key_insight: Neural Operator Splitting learns physically interpretable fractional steps instead of a monolithic fluid update, reducing rollout error in complex geometries.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers fast CFD surrogates for varied geometries, with approximately 1,000× faster per-step inference than the Monte Carlo solver at comparable error levels.
method: Train separate operators on intermediate states from a fractional-step numerical solver.
Use conditional-linear Fourier neural operators to preserve linear state mappings while conditioning nonlinearly on geometry.
Apply symmetry sampling and corrective cycling to mitigate autoregressive error accumulation.
evidence_signal: Across 2D and 3D flows with varying geometries and initial conditions, the full model reduced mean relative L2 rollout error by 68% and 40%, respectively, versus a single full-step neural operator.
watch_item: Training requires solver-generated intermediate states; generalization beyond the evaluated geometries and flow conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
